title: Home conversations record which model wrote them so training exports hold provider answers
request: Close the training-export gap where Home conversations named no model in check, causing 1,276 rows in m4_workflow_llm/understand_problem/v2 to bypass the commercial provider hold as answerer_not_recorded.
spec: home_models() aggregates ok non-shadow conversational model requests per (workspace, draft id), preferring exchange records with provider and source_class. home_answerer() writes check['answerer'] (single, mixed sorted with most restrictive model first, frontier:unknown when draft shows model signs with no captured requests, or rules with no model key). llm.from_draft() and llm.build() populate these fields, and export_chat.provider_of() reads check['answerer'] before check['model'].
plan: G1: add NOT_IN_CONVERSATION, MODEL_QUESTION_SOURCES, home_models, _model_signs, _rank, and home_answerer in dclab_rnd/store/sets/llm.py.
G2: extend llm.from_draft() to accept models and update check via home_answerer(), and build models in llm.build().
G3: update provider_of() in dclab_rnd/store/export_chat.py to read check.get('answerer') before check.get('model').
G4: add 7 unit tests in tests/test_home_answerer.py and 1 end-to-end test in tests/test_store_sets_llm.py, then run the 8-file suite.
G5: check disk and memory, record understand_problem v2 export counts before, rebuild M4/M5 sets via llm.build(), measure export and Home counts after, verify exams clean, and check data_catalog.
G6: record this package, rebuild sft-dev, re-run the 8-file suite, commit all package files, push main and dev, and report results.

decisions.decision: Write rules attribution in check['answerer'] only and never write 'rules' into check['model'].
decisions.why: exchange_answerer reads any check['model'] without provider/source_class as a hosted commercial model (frontier:rules).

decisions.decision: Prefer the most restrictive answerer when a draft mixes multiple models (provider > OpenRouter Qwen > rules) and join them under mixed:...
decisions.why: Guarantees silver_of treats mixed conversations as held until rights review and causes reasoning set builders reading check['model'] to file mixed rows under the provider set.

decisions.decision: Classify drafts that show model signs without captured model requests as frontier:unknown.
decisions.why: Older live_tests workspaces lack captured exchanges for model-run turns; holding them errs on the safe side under the owner's rule.

change: Modified dclab_rnd/store/sets/llm.py (home_models, _model_signs, _rank, home_answerer, from_draft, build) and dclab_rnd/store/export_chat.py (provider_of), added tests/test_home_answerer.py (7 tests) and an end-to-end test in tests/test_store_sets_llm.py, rebuilt M4/M5 sets in the store, and added this dev trajectory record.

findings.defect: Home conversations named no model, so the training export could not hold a provider's answers.
findings.scenario: Exporting m4_workflow_llm/understand_problem/v2 counted 1,276 Home rows as answerer_not_recorded and exported them, including 250 written by Claude (32) or another hosted model (218).
findings.cause: from_draft() in dclab_rnd/store/sets/llm.py never read the model requests logged or exchanged for the draft.
findings.fix: Added home_models() and home_answerer() in dclab_rnd/store/sets/llm.py, wired them into from_draft() and build(), and updated provider_of() in dclab_rnd/store/export_chat.py to read check['answerer'] first.

findings.defect: Many model-run Home conversations have no captured model request at all in the store.
findings.scenario: Drafts from live_tests workspaces recorded agent.mode == 'model', case_state, turns by model or case_agent, or critic/advisory questions without corresponding model_requests records.
findings.cause: Earlier live_tests runs did not capture model request exchanges alongside their draft files.
findings.fix: Added _model_signs() inside home_answerer() to classify drafts showing model activity without captured requests as frontier:unknown (held out of training on the safe side).

measurements.name: The real export of understand_problem v2 before and after the rebuild
measurements.gate: none: real export counts before and after rebuilding M4/M5 sets
measurements.result: Before rebuild: 1432 train and 466 dev exported, held_for_rights claude 2416 (2416 skipped), answerer_not_recorded 1276. After rebuild (546s): 1254 train and 394 dev exported, held_for_rights claude 2448 and frontier 218 (2666 skipped), answerer_not_recorded 0. Home conversation rows in understand_problem v2 (train and dev): rules 1020, frontier 218, claude 32, openrouter 6, NONE 0.
measurements.next: keep held provider rows prepared until the owner sets rights_reviewed: true
limits: old set version understand_problem/v1 is never rebuilt and keeps answerer_not_recorded
requests without a draft id cannot be joined by draft lookup and rely on _model_signs

outcome: Home conversations now record check['answerer'] across the store, reducing answerer_not_recorded in understand_problem v2 from 1,276 to 0, holding all 250 commercial/frontier Home rows (32 claude, 218 frontier), and keeping all 1,020 rules rows and 6 openrouter Qwen rows.
lessons: Never treat a missing model field on a composite conversation object as proof that code rules wrote it; fall back to structural model-run signs before attributing rules.
Keep check['model'] reserved strictly for real model identifiers because exchange_answerer classifies any bare name without provider metadata as a hosted frontier model.
risks: A request with outcome ok may not have reached a turn, so a few rows may be held that need not be.
Requests with no draft id cannot be joined.
understand_problem/v1 (291 old rows) is never rebuilt.
